note: Rulings on out-of-scope differences in an o-1 candidate's receipt. The owner delegated these decisions to the build coordinator (an AI agent); they are sent with the owner's member token and are labelled as delegated, not human. ruling.ps1 turns each rule into a standing predicate and records it through the member HTTP API (record_ruling). Nothing here is a verdict: the gate evaluates each ruling where its field differs, and a probe that fails it becomes violates_ruling. Generated ids, tokens, session cookies, codes and hashes are not ruled here: the protected probe manifest declares them maskable and the gate compares them by format against the base.

rules.label: x-request-id is an opaque random id, not identity
rules.reason: The order does not mention a request id. A random UUID per response identifies the request and carries no user name, so it is accepted. A value that carries a user name is not accepted by this rule and is reported as violating it.

rules.label: an over-limit answer may say when to retry
rules.reason: The order does not mention Retry-After. On a 429 answer it tells the client how many seconds remain in the window (60 on the first over-limit request, 1 at 59999 ms), which is standard HTTP and carries no user data. It is accepted only where the step answers 429; a Retry-After on any other answer violates this ruling.

rules.label: an over-limit answer's body carries only the error
rules.reason: The o-1 scope already allows the 429 body change through its may items; the bounced m-overfit candidate's difference is the same allowed change. (D02Q)

rules.label: an over-limit answer's body carries only the error
rules.reason: The o-1 scope already allows the 429 body change through its may items; the bounced m-overfit candidate's difference is the same allowed change, and its 429 body drops the link fields. (D02Q)
